description: Intact Auto insurance JSON output format configuration

last_name.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's last name (surname) from the MVR field labeled 'Name' / 'Name :' ONLY — MVR is the authoritative source (not the Application form). ⚠️ NEVER use Birth Date, Expiry Date, Issue Date, BirDt, ExpDt, Height, Gender, Address, or ANY date value as a name — date_of_birth is a separate field. Example (Ontario MVR): 'Name : HE, XINYI' with 'Birth Date : 21/11/1992' on another line → last_name='HE', first_name='XINYI' (NOT '21/11/1992'). ⚠️ MVR NAME FORMAT (HARD RULE): MVR prints names as LAST, FIRST[, MIDDLE] using commas as the ONLY delimiter. Case 1 — 'LAST, FIRST, MIDDLE': last_name = first part; ignore middle. Case 2 — 'LAST, FIRST': last_name = first part. Case 3 — last name only ('LAST' or 'LAST,'): last_name = that text AND first_name = same text. NEVER split on whitespace. Examples: 'HE, XINYI' → last_name='HE'; 'SINGH, NAVDEEP' → last_name='SINGH'.

first_name.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's first name from the MVR field labeled 'Name' / 'Name :' ONLY — MVR is the authoritative source (not the Application form). ⚠️ NEVER put Birth Date, Expiry Date, or any other date into first_name — dates belong in date_of_birth and other date fields only. Example: 'Name : HE, XINYI' with Birth Date 21/11/1992 elsewhere → first_name='XINYI' (never '21/11/1992'). ⚠️ MVR NAME FORMAT (HARD RULE): LAST, FIRST[, MIDDLE] — comma is the ONLY delimiter. Case 1 — three parts: first_name = second part (ignore middle). Case 2 — two parts: first_name = second part. Case 3 — last name only: first_name = same as last_name. NEVER split on whitespace. Examples: 'HE, XINYI' → first_name='XINYI'; 'WANG, AI, LEE' → first_name='AI'.

gender.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's gender. Priority: first check application form, if not found check other documents. Must match one of the options: Female, Male, or X.

date_of_birth.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's date of birth. Priority: first check application form, if not found check other documents. Convert to YYYY-MM-DD format.
date_of_birth.description: Applicant's date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format

marital_status.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's marital status. Priority: first check application form, if not found check other documents. Must match one of the options: Divorced, Married, Single, or Widow.

postal_code.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's postal code from the application (Canadian format X9X9X9, e.g. 'M4C 5L6' or 'M4C5L6').
postal_code.description: Applicant postal code in Canadian format X9X9X9

full_address.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's full mailing address from the application (street/unit, city, province) without postal code, e.g. '511-5 Massey Sq, East York, ON'.
full_address.description: Applicant full address (street, city, province — no postal code)

phone.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's primary telephone number from the application (home, cell, or main contact). Output digits only — no hyphens, spaces, parentheses, or other separators (e.g. '4165550100' not '416-555-0100').
phone.description: Applicant primary phone number (digits only, no separators)

email.extraction_logic: Extract the applicant's email address from the application. Use the address exactly as printed.

broker_number.extraction_logic: Extract the broker number from the application form. The broker code may start with a capital letter (e.g., 'X40460', 'A12345'). If it starts with a capital letter, ignore that letter and extract only the numeric part. Output should be 5 digits (e.g., 'X40460' should become '40460').
broker_number.description: 5-digit broker number (numeric part only, ignore leading capital letter if present)

edi_client_code.extraction_logic: Extract the EDI client code from the application form. Look for 'Code:' label followed by the code value (e.g., 'Code: ALEE01' should extract 'ALEE01').

policy_effective_date.description: Policy effective date in YYYY-MM-DD format

risk.description: Risk information - array of vehicles. Extract ALL vehicles found in documents. Each element represents one vehicle.
risk.extraction_logic: Extract ALL vehicles (risks) found in the documents. Each vehicle should be a separate element in the array. If only one vehicle is found, the array should contain one element. Each risk element should contain all the risk fields for that specific vehicle—including the nested `interest` object for that vehicle's loan/lease/lienholder information.

risk_type.extraction_logic: Extract the risk type from documents for THIS specific vehicle. If there is no clear evidence indicating a different vehicle type (ATV, ANT, CLA, MCY, MHO, SNO, PPT), default to 'PPV' (Private Passenger Vehicle).

serial_number.extraction_logic: Extract the vehicle VIN (Vehicle Identification Number) for THIS specific vehicle from the quote document. VIN is typically 17 characters long.

model.extraction_logic: Extract the full vehicle model descriptor for THIS specific vehicle. Include as much detail as available, ideally in a format like '2022 Toyota Corolla SE Hatchback 5dr FWD 2.0L I4'. If year/make/model/trim/body/drivetrain are available, combine them into one concise string.
model.description: Detailed vehicle model descriptor (year + make + model + trim/body/drivetrain when available)

condition_when_purchased_or_leased.description: Condition of the vehicle when purchased or leased
options: Demo More than or Equal to 5,000 KM

date_of_purchase_or_lease.description: Date of purchase or lease in YYYY-MM-DD format

winter_tires.description: Whether the vehicle has winter tires

unrepaired_damage.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific vehicle. If there is no clear evidence indicating unrepaired damage, default to 'No'.

vehicle_rebuilt.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific vehicle. If there is no clear evidence indicating the vehicle has been rebuilt, default to 'No'.
vehicle_rebuilt.description: Whether the vehicle has been rebuilt

vehicle_photos_received.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific vehicle. If there is no clear evidence indicating vehicle photos have been received, default to 'No'.
vehicle_photos_received.description: Whether vehicle photos have been received

vehicle_modified_or_accessories.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific vehicle. If there is no clear evidence indicating the vehicle has been modified or has accessories, default to 'No'.
vehicle_modified_or_accessories.description: Whether the vehicle has been modified or has accessories

interest.description: Per-vehicle loan/lease/lienholder (interest) for THIS risk only. ⚠️ APPLICATION FORM ONLY — NEVER Quote, NEVER MVR, NEVER Autoplus. On Application (OAF 1 Section 3 'Described Automobile'), find THIS vehicle's Auto No. row under 'Lienholder Name & Postal Address' (Auto No. 1 = first risk, etc.). Quote '#23a Lienholder Protection' is insurance coverage, NOT the lender — ignore it for interest.

has_loan.extraction_logic: For THIS specific vehicle, determine whether it has a loan, finance, lien, or lease. ⚠️ APPLICATION FORM ONLY — DO NOT read or use the Quote document for this field (Quote does not list the lender; '#23a Lienholder Protection' is a coverage line, not a loan). In Application_Form Section 3 (Described Automobile), find 'Lienholder Name & Postal Address' and match THIS vehicle to its Auto No. (first vehicle = Auto No. 1, second = Auto No. 2, ...). If that Application row contains a finance company name and/or mailing address (e.g. '1. TD Auto Finance - PO Box 4086, Station A, Toronto, ON, M5W 5K3'), has_loan MUST be 'Yes'. Do NOT output has_loan='No' when that Application row is populated. Only output 'No' when the Application lienholder row for this Auto No. is blank/empty. IMPORTANT: If has_loan is 'No', omit type_of_interest, company_name, address, postal_code from this interest object.
has_loan.description: Whether this vehicle has a loan or interest or finance or lease (Yes when Application lienholder row is filled)

type_of_interest.extraction_logic: For THIS vehicle, extract from Application_Form ONLY (never Quote). On Application Section 3, if the vehicle is a lease, select 'Lessor'; for loan/finance/lien, select 'Lienholder'. Only include this field if has_loan is 'Yes'.
type_of_interest.description: Type of interest for interested party

company_name.extraction_logic: For THIS vehicle, extract the lienholder/lessor company name from the Application ONLY — the 'Lienholder Name & Postal Address' row for this vehicle's Auto No. (e.g. Auto No. 1 → 'TD Auto Finance' at the start of that cell). The company name is the finance institution — NEVER the applicant/driver name (e.g. NOT 'TARIQ, HUMAIL'). Match to the corporate list using fuzzy matching. If no list match, output the name exactly as printed on Application. Only when has_loan is 'Yes'.
options: Fédération des Caisses Desjardins du Québec

address.extraction_logic: For THIS vehicle, extract the complete lienholder/lessor mailing address from the Application ONLY — the 'Lienholder Name & Postal Address' row for this Auto No. Capture the FULL address exactly as shown after the company name. Formats vary: PO Box, street address, station, suite, city, province (e.g. 'PO Box 4086, Station A, Toronto, ON' or '123 Main St, Suite 400, Calgary, AB'). Do NOT use Quote/MVR/Autoplus for this field. Do NOT include the company name. Do NOT include the postal code here (use interest.postal_code). Only include this field if has_loan is 'Yes'.
address.description: Full postal address of the lienholder/lessor (without postal code)

postal_code.extraction_logic: For THIS vehicle, extract the Canadian postal code from the Application lienholder row only (format X9X9X9, e.g. 'M5W 5K3' → 'M5W5K3'). Only include this field if has_loan is 'Yes'.
postal_code.description: Lienholder/lessor postal code (Canadian format), separate from address

driver.description: Driver information - array of drivers. Extract ALL drivers found in documents. Each element represents one driver.
driver.extraction_logic: Extract ALL drivers found in the documents. Each driver should be a separate element in the array. If only one driver is found, the array should contain one element. Each driver element should contain all the driver fields for that specific driver. IMPORTANT for identity fields (last_name, first_name, gender, date_of_birth, marital_status, postal_code, full_address): include them ONLY for the second, third, fourth, ... driver (array index 1, 2, 3, ...). For the FIRST driver (index 0), OMIT these seven fields—they duplicate applicant_information at the root. For each additional driver, fill these with THAT driver's personal details and address from the policy; if the driver shares the same household as the applicant, you may use the same postal_code and full_address as applicant_information.

last_name.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: last name from THIS driver's MVR 'Name' field only. Omit on first driver (index 0). NEVER use Birth Date or any date as a name. MVR format LAST, FIRST[, MIDDLE] — comma only delimiter. 'HE, XINYI' → last_name='HE'.
last_name.description: Additional driver's last name (omit on first driver in array)

first_name.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: first name from THIS driver's MVR 'Name' field only. Omit on first driver (index 0). NEVER put Birth Date or any date into first_name. 'HE, XINYI' → first_name='XINYI'.
first_name.description: Additional driver's first name (omit on first driver in array)

gender.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: Female, Male, or X. Omit on the first driver (index 0).

date_of_birth.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit on the first driver (index 0).
date_of_birth.description: Additional driver's date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format

marital_status.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: Divorced, Married, Single, or Widow. Omit on the first driver (index 0).

postal_code.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: this driver's postal code (Canadian X9X9X9). If same household as applicant, repeat applicant_information.postal_code. Omit on the first driver (index 0).

full_address.extraction_logic: For drivers at index 1+ only: full address like '168 Trail Ridge Lane, Markham, ON'. If same household, repeat applicant_information.full_address. Omit on the first driver (index 0).

student.description: Whether THIS specific driver is a student

driver_training_certificate.extraction_logic: Whether THIS specific driver has a driver training certificate. ⚠️ SOURCE: Quote document ONLY — ignore Application, MVR, AutoPlus, and DIS discount lines (e.g. 'Discount - Graduated License Holder included' does NOT affect this field). On the Quote, find the 'Driver Training' field for THIS driver in the Drivers section. ⚠️ LAYOUT: the Quote often prints the value ABOVE the label (not beside it), e.g. 'No' on one line then 'Driver Training' on the next, or 'Yes' then 'Driver Training' — read the Yes/No value paired with that label (also accept horizontal 'Driver Training: Yes/No' if present). Output 'Yes' only when that Quote value is explicitly Yes, Y, or an affirmative checked indicator; output 'No' when it reads No, N, or is blank/absent on the Quote for this driver. Do NOT infer from age, licence class, another driver's value, or any non-Quote document. When the Quote shows no Driver Training field for this driver, output 'No'.
driver_training_certificate.description: Driver training certificate Yes/No — from Quote 'Driver Training' only (value often printed directly above the label); ignore Application and discounts

licence_class.extraction_logic: Extract THIS specific driver's licence class from documents. IMPORTANT: Based on the selected licence_class, only include the corresponding date fields. For G-class licences: if licence_class is 'G1', only include g1_class_date_licensed; if licence_class is 'G2', include g1_class_date_licensed and g2_class_date_licensed (but NOT g_class_date_licensed); if licence_class is 'G', include all three: g1_class_date_licensed, g2_class_date_licensed, and g_class_date_licensed.

g_class_date_licensed.extraction_logic: Extract the G Class date licensed for THIS specific driver. ⚠️ COLUMN ALIGNMENT (HARD RULE): The Quote / Application driver block prints licence dates as a row of THREE dates immediately under the headers `Licence Class | Date G | Date G2 | Date G1` (in this LEFT-TO-RIGHT order). The FIRST date (under 'Date G') is g_class_date_licensed, the SECOND (under 'Date G2') is g2_class_date_licensed, the THIRD (under 'Date G1') is g1_class_date_licensed. Read each value strictly from the cell directly below its header — do NOT swap, reorder, or replace these values with dates from MVR or any other source. ⚠️ DATE FORMAT: dates print as MM/DD/YYYY (US-style) in this section, so '10/20/1999' = 1999-10-20 (October 20), '09/14/1998' = 1998-09-14, NOT day-first. Convert each printed date to YYYY-MM-DD verbatim from these cells. ONLY include this field if licence_class is 'G'. Do NOT include if licence_class is 'G1' or 'G2'.
g_class_date_licensed.description: G Class - Date Licensed in YYYY-MM-DD format (read from the 'Date G' column directly under that header; MM/DD/YYYY in source)

g2_class_date_licensed.extraction_logic: Extract the G2 Class date licensed for THIS specific driver. ⚠️ COLUMN ALIGNMENT (HARD RULE): Read the value strictly from the cell directly below the 'Date G2' header in the row `Licence Class | Date G | Date G2 | Date G1`. Do NOT pull this from the 'Date G' or 'Date G1' column, and do NOT replace with a date from MVR or any other source. ⚠️ DATE FORMAT: source prints MM/DD/YYYY (US-style), so '09/14/1998' = 1998-09-14, NOT 1998-04-09. Include this field if licence_class is 'G2' or 'G'. Do NOT include if licence_class is 'G1'.
g2_class_date_licensed.description: G2 Class - Date Licensed in YYYY-MM-DD format (read from the 'Date G2' column directly under that header; MM/DD/YYYY in source)

g1_class_date_licensed.extraction_logic: Extract the G1 Class date licensed for THIS specific driver. ⚠️ COLUMN ALIGNMENT (HARD RULE): Read the value strictly from the cell directly below the 'Date G1' header in the row `Licence Class | Date G | Date G2 | Date G1`. Do NOT pull this from 'Date G' or 'Date G2'. ⚠️ DATE FORMAT: source prints MM/DD/YYYY (US-style), so '08/11/1994' = 1994-08-11. Include this field if licence_class is 'G1', 'G2', or 'G'.
g1_class_date_licensed.description: G1 Class - Date Licensed in YYYY-MM-DD format (read from the 'Date G1' column directly under that header; MM/DD/YYYY in source)

MVR_report_status.extraction_logic: Set MVR report status for THIS specific driver based on conviction result. If this driver has no conviction, select 'received-clean'. If this driver has any conviction detail/code (not 'No'), select 'received-with detail'.
MVR_report_status.description: MVR report status for THIS specific driver

MVR_request_date_time.extraction_logic: For THIS specific driver, locate the MVR document that belongs to this driver (match by driver's first/last name appearing in the MVR text), then read the date from the upper-right header at the very top of that MVR, which looks like '*** MOTOR VEHICLE RECORD - YYYY/MM/DD ***'. Do NOT use any other date inside the MVR body. Output in YYYY-MM-DD format.
MVR_request_date_time.description: MVR's Request Date/Time in YYYY-MM-DD format for THIS specific driver, taken from the upper-right header '*** MOTOR VEHICLE RECORD - YYYY/MM/DD ***' of THIS driver's MVR

Consent_Date.extraction_logic: For THIS specific driver, compare two dates and choose the EARLIER one: (1) the MVR header date in the upper-right corner of THIS driver's MVR document, in the form '*** MOTOR VEHICLE RECORD - YYYY/MM/DD ***' (match the MVR to this driver by first/last name; do NOT use any other date inside the MVR body); (2) the AutoPlus 'Report Date'. When multiple MVR documents are present, each driver MUST use the header date from their own MVR (not the global earliest). Output the earlier date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
Consent_Date.description: Consent date in YYYY-MM-DD format for THIS specific driver (earlier of THIS driver's MVR upper-right header date and AutoPlus Report Date)

insurance_history_report_status.extraction_logic: Extract from dash/autoplus documents for THIS specific driver. Check if the insurance history report is detected or has specific content. If dash/autoplus documents are missing (not provided) for this driver, treat it as no insurance history record and select 'Not Found'. Select 'Not Found' if not detected in dash/autoplus, 'Not Ordered' if not ordered, 'Received' if received, or 'Ordered - Pending' if ordered but pending.
insurance_history_report_status.description: Insurance history report status for THIS specific driver

insurance_history_report_request_date.extraction_logic: Extract the insurance history report request date for THIS specific driver. If not found in documents, use the same value as 'MVR_request_date_time' (MVR's Request Date/Time).
insurance_history_report_request_date.description: Insurance History Report Request Date in YYYY-MM-DD format for THIS specific driver

convictions.extraction_logic: Extract from MVR documents for THIS specific driver. If convictions are found, analyze the conviction description in the MVR document and match it to the most appropriate conviction code from the options list. Each code represents a specific violation type (e.g., 'ALCAF' = 'Accompanying Driver - Fail or Refuse to Provide Breath Sample', 'CDR' = 'Careless Driving', 'SP50M' = 'Speeding - Less than 50 KM over Speed Limit'). Select the code that best matches the conviction description found in the MVR. If no convictions are found in the MVR, select 'No'.
convictions.description: THIS specific driver's conviction type. Select 'No' if no convictions found.

licence_suspensions.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific driver. Default to 'No' unless there is clear evidence in the documents indicating that the driver has licence suspensions. Only select 'Yes' if there is explicit information about licence suspensions.
licence_suspensions.description: Whether THIS specific driver has licence suspensions

lapse_in_insurance.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific driver. Set to 'Yes' if ONE OR MORE lapses appear in the AutoPlus / Application 'Lapses' section for this driver. If 'Yes', the parallel arrays `lapse_in_insurance_description`, `lapse_start`, `lapse_end` MUST also be included in the output, each with one entry per lapse (same length, same order).
lapse_in_insurance.description: Whether there is a lapse in insurance for THIS specific driver

lapse_in_insurance_description.extraction_logic: Only extract when 'lapse_in_insurance' is 'Yes'. ⚠️ ALWAYS OUTPUT AS A JSON ARRAY (never a single string), one element per lapse for THIS driver, even if there is only one lapse (then output a one-element array). Each element must be one of the options. Multiple lapses are common for a single driver — extract EVERY lapse row found in the AutoPlus / Application 'Lapses' section in chronological order; do NOT collapse multiple lapses into one. The arrays `lapse_in_insurance_description`, `lapse_start`, `lapse_end` MUST be the same length and aligned by index (index i = the i-th lapse). Choose the most appropriate description from the options for each lapse.
lapse_in_insurance_description.description: Description for EACH insurance lapse for THIS specific driver — array of strings, one per lapse, aligned with lapse_start / lapse_end by index

lapse_start.extraction_logic: Only extract when 'lapse_in_insurance' is 'Yes'. ⚠️ ALWAYS OUTPUT AS A JSON ARRAY of YYYY-MM-DD strings, one element per lapse, aligned by index with `lapse_in_insurance_description` and `lapse_end`. Map each element from the Lapses section 'Date' (lapse start) field for that specific lapse on THIS driver. If a single lapse exists, still output a one-element array.
lapse_start.description: Lapse start date(s) for THIS specific driver — array of YYYY-MM-DD strings, one per lapse, aligned with lapse_in_insurance_description / lapse_end by index

lapse_end.extraction_logic: Only extract when 'lapse_in_insurance' is 'Yes'. ⚠️ ALWAYS OUTPUT AS A JSON ARRAY of YYYY-MM-DD strings, one element per lapse, aligned by index with `lapse_in_insurance_description` and `lapse_start`. Map each element from the Lapses section 'Re-Instate Date' (lapse end) field for that specific lapse on THIS driver. If a lapse has no Re-Instate Date printed (e.g. 'No Automobile' lapse covering the gap up to the policy effective date), output null at that index — keep the array length aligned. Do NOT mix multiple lapse ends into one string.
lapse_end.description: Lapse end date(s) for THIS specific driver — array of YYYY-MM-DD strings (or null per element when missing), one per lapse, aligned with lapse_in_insurance_description / lapse_start by index

insured_without_interruption_since.description: Insured Without Interruption Since in YYYY-MM-DD format for THIS specific driver

risk_type.extraction_logic: Extract from documents for THIS specific driver. Default to 'Private Passenger Vehicle' unless there is clear evidence indicating a different vehicle type (All terrain Vehicle, Antique, Classic, Motorcycle, Motorhome, Snowmobile, or Trailer). Only select a different option if there is explicit information about the vehicle type.
risk_type.description: Risk type or vehicle type for THIS specific driver

previous_insurer.extraction_logic: Extract the previous insurer name for THIS specific driver. SOURCE PRIORITY: (1) Prefer the 'Insurance Company' value printed on the APPLICATION form under the applicant's most recent automobile insurance (the row that also shows Policy No. and Expiry Date) whenever that field is present and legible. (2) If that field is missing or blank on the Application, use AutoPlus / DASH / HITS or other supporting documents. After you have a chosen name, match it to the dropdown list: prefer an exact match, then case-insensitive match, then fuzzy match (e.g. 'BMO' -> 'Bank of Montreal', 'RBC' -> 'Royal Bank of Canada'). If a match is found, output the exact name from the list. If no match is found and there is clearly no prior insurer, output 'No Prior Insurer'.
previous_insurer.description: Previous insurer name for THIS specific driver

expiry_date.extraction_logic: Extract the expiry date from the previous insurance information in documents for THIS specific driver. This is the end date of the previous insurance policy in YYYY-MM-DD format.
expiry_date.description: Expiry date in YYYY-MM-DD format (from previous insurance) for THIS specific driver

previous_insurer_policy_number.extraction_logic: Extract the policy number from the previous insurance information in documents for THIS specific driver.
previous_insurer_policy_number.description: Previous insurer policy number (from previous insurance) for THIS specific driver

number_of_years_with_previous_insurer.extraction_logic: Calculate the number of years for THIS specific driver by subtracting the previous insurance effective date from the expiry_date. Use rounding up (ceiling) - if it's more than 3 years even by one day, it counts as 4 years. The result must be an integer. For example: if effective date is 2020-01-01 and expiry date is 2023-01-02, that's 3 years and 1 day, which rounds up to 4 years.
number_of_years_with_previous_insurer.description: Number of years with previous insurer (calculated, rounded up to integer) for THIS specific driver

assignment.description: Assignment information. Includes per-vehicle driver usage (vehicle_1, vehicle_2, ...) aligned with quote 'Vehicle N of M' blocks and their Drivers lists, plus vehicle use and mileage fields. ⚠️ USAGE TABLE READING (Intact Quote): Primary Use / Annual km / Business km / Daily km are often OCR'd as a VERTICAL value-above-label stack (not one horizontal row). Read each field from the text line directly ABOVE its label; see km_toward_work extraction_logic for the full example.

vehicle_1.extraction_logic: For the FIRST vehicle on the quote (e.g. 'Vehicle 1 of M'), output an object whose keys are driver_1, driver_2, driver_3, ... in the SAME order as drivers listed under THAT vehicle's Drivers section. Each driver_k MUST be an object with: (1) name: string — full name as printed (e.g. 'Ai Wang'); strip trailing role tags like '(Prn)' / '(Occ)' from the name value if they appear only as labels. (2) percentage_of_use: integer 0–100. DEFAULT (covers most quotes): the quote usually only indicates WHO is Principal vs Occasional via labels like (Prn) and (Occ), NOT numeric percentages — in that case you MUST fill percentage_of_use using ONLY these FIXED rules by driver count N on THIS vehicle: N=1 → 100 for the sole driver. N=2 → Prn 60, Occ 40. N=3 → Prn 60, each Occ 20. N=4 → Prn 70, each Occ 10. N=5 → Prn 60, each Occ 10. Match each value to the correct person by (Prn)/(Occ), not by list position alone. EXCEPTION (rare): if the quote explicitly prints a numeric 'Percentage of Use (%)' (or equivalent) per driver, use those printed values instead of the fixed rules. If N>5: use printed percentages when present; otherwise Prn 60 and split remaining 40 equally among Occ drivers (integers summing to 100). Omit vehicle_1 entirely only if the quote provides no per-vehicle driver listing for vehicle 1.
vehicle_1.description: Vehicle 1 driver usage: nested driver_1, driver_2, ... each with name and percentage_of_use (0-100); default % grid by Prn/Occ count per rules in extraction_logic.

vehicle_2.extraction_logic: Same structure and rules as vehicle_1, but for the SECOND vehicle on the quote ('Vehicle 2 of M'). Omit if there is no second vehicle.
vehicle_2.description: Vehicle 2 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

vehicle_3.extraction_logic: Same as vehicle_1 for the third vehicle. Omit if fewer than three vehicles.
vehicle_3.description: Vehicle 3 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

vehicle_4.extraction_logic: Same as vehicle_1 for the fourth vehicle. Omit if fewer than four vehicles.
vehicle_4.description: Vehicle 4 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

vehicle_5.extraction_logic: Same as vehicle_1 for the fifth vehicle. Omit if fewer than five vehicles.
vehicle_5.description: Vehicle 5 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

vehicle_6.extraction_logic: Same as vehicle_1 for the sixth vehicle. Omit if fewer than six vehicles.
vehicle_6.description: Vehicle 6 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

vehicle_7.extraction_logic: Same as vehicle_1 for the seventh vehicle. Omit if fewer than seven vehicles.
vehicle_7.description: Vehicle 7 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

vehicle_8.extraction_logic: Same as vehicle_1 for the eighth vehicle. Omit if fewer than eight vehicles.
vehicle_8.description: Vehicle 8 driver usage (same shape as vehicle_1).

type_of_use.extraction_logic: Extract primary use for THIS vehicle from the Quote usage block. ⚠️ VERTICAL STACKED LAYOUT (COMMON): OCR often prints the value on the line ABOVE the label, e.g. 'Pleasure' then 'Primary Use' (not 'Pleasure' on the same line as headers). Read the non-empty line directly above 'Primary Use' that is not another header (Annual km, Business km, Daily km). If uncertain or not found, default to 'Pleasure'.
type_of_use.description: Type of use for the vehicle

km_toward_work.extraction_logic:
Extract kilometers driven toward work (Daily km) for THIS vehicle from the Quote. ⚠️ VERTICAL STACKED LAYOUT (MOST COMMON ON INTACT QUOTE OCR): fields appear value-above-label, column by column — NOT as one horizontal row. Typical OCR order:
Pleasure
Primary Use
10000
Annual km
Business km
6
Daily km
For km_toward_work: find the line 'Daily km', then read the nearest non-empty line ABOVE it that is NOT another header label (Primary Use, Annual km, Business km). In the example above that line is '6' → output 6. ⚠️ HARD RULES: (1) Small single-digit values (4, 6, 8, 10) are VALID — never replace with 0. (2) Do NOT infer 0 from an empty Business km column; Business km blank does NOT mean Daily km is 0. (3) Only output 0 when the line immediately above 'Daily km' is another header label (cell blank) or 'Daily km' is absent. (4) Horizontal layout fallback: if values share one row under headers `Primary Use | Annual km | Business km | Daily km`, read the number under the Daily km column only. Priority: Quote first. Output integer, no units.
km_toward_work.description: Daily km — read the number on the line directly above the 'Daily km' label in vertical OCR (e.g. 6 above 'Daily km'); never default to 0 when that line is a number

annual_km.extraction_logic: Extract annual kilometers for THIS vehicle from the Quote usage block. In the vertical stacked OCR layout, read the non-empty line directly above the 'Annual km' label (e.g. '10000' above 'Annual km'). Horizontal fallback: number under the Annual km column header. Priority: Quote first.

annual_business_km.extraction_logic: Extract annual business kilometers for THIS vehicle. In vertical stacked OCR, read the line directly above 'Business km' ONLY if that line is a number (not another header label); if the line above is 'Annual km' or another label, the Business km cell is blank → output 0. IMPORTANT: If type_of_use is 'Pleasure', annual_business_km must always be 0. Priority: Quote first.

automobile_rented_or_leased_to_others.extraction_logic: If there is no clear evidence that the automobile is rented or leased to others, must select 'No'. Only select 'Yes' if there is explicit evidence in the documents.
automobile_rented_or_leased_to_others.description: Whether the automobile is rented or leased to others

automobile_used_to_carry_passengers_for_.extraction_logic: If there is no clear evidence that the automobile is used to carry passengers for compensation or hire, must select 'No'. Only select 'Yes' if there is explicit evidence in the documents.
automobile_used_to_carry_passengers_for_.description: Whether the automobile is used to carry passengers for compensation or hire

automobile_carry_explosives_or_radioacti.extraction_logic: If there is no clear evidence that the automobile carries explosives or radioactive materials, must select 'No'. Only select 'Yes' if there is explicit evidence in the documents.
automobile_carry_explosives_or_radioacti.description: Whether the automobile carries explosives or radioactive materials

has_claim.extraction_logic: If 'No' is selected, all other fields in the 'claim' section (date_of_loss, at_fault, cause_of_loss, total_amount_paid, coverage, assigned_vehicle) should not be present in the output. Only extract other claim fields if 'Yes' is selected. If 'Yes', extract ALL claims found in the documents - there can be multiple claims, and each claim should have corresponding entries in all claim fields (arrays should have the same length, with index i representing claim i).

date_of_loss.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Extract ALL dates of loss for ALL claims found in the documents. Each date should be in YYYY-MM-DD format. Output as an array, where each element corresponds to one claim. If there are multiple claims, this array should have multiple elements.
date_of_loss.description: Date of loss in YYYY-MM-DD format (array - one element per claim)

at_fault.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Extract whether each claim was at fault. Output as an array, where each element corresponds to one claim. The array length should match the number of claims found.
at_fault.description: Whether at fault (array - one element per claim)

cause_of_loss.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Select the most appropriate cause of loss from the options for EACH claim found. Output as an array, where each element corresponds to one claim. The array length should match the number of claims found.
cause_of_loss.description: Cause of loss (array - one element per claim)
options: Enter or Exit Driveway or Parking Lot
INS Wrong Way One Way Street
TP Wrong Way One Way Street

total_amount_paid.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Extract the total amount paid for EACH claim found. Output as an array of numbers, where each element corresponds to one claim. The array length should match the number of claims found.
total_amount_paid.description: Total amount paid in currency (array - one element per claim)

coverage.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Select the coverage type for EACH claim found. Output as an array, where each element corresponds to one claim. The array length should match the number of claims found.
coverage.description: Coverage type (array - one element per claim)

assigned_vehicle.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Extract the vehicle information for EACH claim found (e.g., vehicle description, VIN, or vehicle identifier). Output as an array of strings, where each element corresponds to one claim. The array length should match the number of claims found.
assigned_vehicle.description: The vehicle that this claim is assigned to (array - one element per claim)

assigned_driver.extraction_logic: Only extract if has_claim is 'Yes'. Extract the driver information for EACH claim found (e.g., driver full name or clear driver identifier). Output as an array of strings, where each element corresponds to one claim. The array length should match the number of claims found and should align by index with date_of_loss/at_fault/cause_of_loss/total_amount_paid/coverage/assigned_vehicle.
assigned_driver.description: The driver that this claim is assigned to (array - one element per claim)

limit.extraction_logic: Extract from the quote document. Look for the value following 'Bodily Injury'. Convert abbreviations: 1m = 1000000, 2m = 2000000, etc. Select the matching value from the dropdown options.
limit.description: Limit amount in currency (typically found after 'Bodily Injury' in quote document)

additional_coverages.extraction_logic: Mirror the Intact Quote line-by-line in this array. MANDATORY sources: (1) the main coverage/premium table (each row under coverages such as Bodily Injury / Prop. Damage, Property Damage, Direct Compensation, Accident Benefits, All Perils, Uninsured Automobile, #20 Loss of Use, #23a Lienholder Protection, #44 Family Protection, Service Fee, and any other rows on that table); (2) the DIS (discounts) sidebar/list (e.g. 'Discount - Winter Tire included', 'Discount - Hybrid and Electric Vehicle included', 'Discount - Graduated License Holder included'). Output ONE array element per quote coverage row AND per DIS discount — ⚠️ NEVER omit a coverage or discount because its limit/deductible/premium is 0; include every row that appears on the quote. Do not skip a table row just because it is also filled in coverages.limit, dcpd_deductible, all_perils_or_collision_or_upset, or other dedicated fields; those fields AND this array must both reflect the quote. Use the coverage description text exactly as printed on the quote (normalize #20 to match quote wording). For the limit/deductible column (middle column, NOT PRIN./TOTALS premium): use 'Name: Value' when a limit/deductible is shown — including 0 (e.g. 'Direct Compensation: 0', 'Property Damage: 0'); convert 1M/1 m = 1000000, 1K = 1000, etc.; if the limit/deductible column is blank or 'Inc.' only, output the name alone. Always include every DIS discount bullet as its own entry (name only, even when the discount amount is $0). Do NOT use section_optional_coverages or accident_benefits_standard_benefits. Never put premium dollars in this array — only coverage name and limit/deductible (including 0 when printed).
additional_coverages.description: Every Quote coverage table row plus every DIS discount line — one element per row; never drop entries because the limit/deductible is 0

dcpd_deductible.description: Direct Compensation - Property Damage (DCPD) deductible amount

all_perils_or_collision_or_upset.description: ALL Perils OR Collision or Upset coverage type

all_perils_or_collision_or_upset_deducti.description: Deductible amount for ALL Perils OR Collision or Upset coverage

specified_perils_or_comprehensive.description: Specified Perils OR Comprehensive coverage type

specified_perils_or_comprehensive_deduct.description: Deductible amount for Specified Perils OR Comprehensive coverage

automobile_insurance_cancelled_or_refuse.extraction_logic: If there is no clear evidence that automobile insurance was cancelled or refused in the last 3 years, must select 'No'. Only select 'Yes' if there is explicit evidence in the documents.
automobile_insurance_cancelled_or_refuse.description: Automobile Insurance Cancelled or Refused in Last 3 Years

insured_with_broker_since.extraction_logic: Use the Quote document only. Find the label 'Brokerage Insured' (often italic, near the quote header/summary). If a date is printed next to or on the line after that label, extract it and output YYYY-MM-DD. If the Brokerage Insured value is blank/empty (label present but no date), use term.policy_effective_date as insured_with_broker_since. Do not invent a date from Application or MVR when Quote shows Brokerage Insured empty.
insured_with_broker_since.description: Insured With Broker Since (YYYY-MM-DD) — Quote Brokerage Insured date, or policy_effective_date when Quote field is empty

ubi_consent.extraction_logic: Use fuzzy document understanding to determine UBI consent. Strong Yes signals include Quote mentions like 'W0048 - MY DRIVE-ACTIVATION (NEW BUS ONLY) INCLUDED' or equivalent MY DRIVE activation wording, and Application clues such as 'Number of Telematics: 1' (especially near the end pages). Treat semantically equivalent wording/OCR variants as valid evidence. If clear UBI/telematics enrollment evidence is present, select 'Yes'; otherwise select 'No'.

named_insureds_have_additional_policies_.extraction_logic: Always select 'No' for this field, regardless of document content.
named_insureds_have_additional_policies_.description: Do the Named Insureds have additional policies with Intact Financial Corporation

premium_on_quote.description: Premium on quote — final total automobile policy premium as printed on the Quote document.
premium_on_quote.extraction_logic: Use ONLY the Quote document (ignore Application, MVR, AutoPlus for this value). Find the final policy premium the insured pays — the bottom-line total on the quote summary, often labeled 'Total Premium', 'Annual Premium', 'Total Policy Premium', 'Premium', 'Total', or similar on the last premium/payment summary section. If the quote shows per-vehicle premiums and a policy-level grand total, use the grand total. If only one clear total appears, use that. Preserve the value as printed (digits; $ and commas optional if shown). Do not substitute per-coverage line amounts. If no total can be identified on the quote, output null. IMPORTANT: emit this value as a single JSON string at the root key `premium_on_quote` only — do NOT nest it inside an object (no `total` or other wrapper).
